paper.title: Few-for-Many Best-Arm Identification in Multi-Objective Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Few-for-many BAI with known objective groups
unmapped: Multi-objective bandit: each pull reveals an M-dimensional reward vector (all objectives observed)
Fixed-confidence identification of one representative arm per known objective group, minimizing the worst weighted degradation R_q(a) = max_{m in G_q} lambda_m (mu_m^* - mu_{a,m})
Known weights lambda_m and known partition of objectives
Each objective has a unique best arm; means in [0,1]
Noise sigma^2-sub-Gaussian conditionally on history; coordinates may be dependent
settings.definition_quote: In the known-group setting, objectives are partitioned in advance, and all objectives in a group share one representative arm. ... For every group q and arm a, we define the group coverage loss as R_q(a)=max_{m in G_q} lambda_m(mu_m^* - mu_{a,m}). ... the identification target is a_G^* = (a_1^*,...,a_Q^*), a_q^* = argmin_a R_q(a).

settings.name_in_paper: Few-for-many BAI with latent objective groups
unmapped: Multi-objective bandit with M-dimensional vector rewards
Identify the size-L arm set S_L^* minimizing Phi(S) = max_m lambda_m (mu_m^* - max_{a in S} mu_{a,m}); representative budget L known
Each objective has a unique best arm; means in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: In the latent-group setting, the objective partition is not known in advance. Instead, the learner is given a representative budget 1<=L<<M and seeks L arms that jointly provide good coverage of all objectives ... S_L^* = argmin_{S in S_L} Phi(S).

settings.name_in_paper: Latent-group few-for-many BAI with Gaussian rewards
unmapped: Multi-objective: each pull yields r_t ~ N(mu_a, sigma^2 I_M)
Identify the unique optimal size-L representative set S_L^*
settings.definition_quote: We consider Gaussian rewards, where each pull of arm a in [K] yields an independent observation r_t ~ N(mu_a, sigma^2 I_M). ... let S_L^*(mu) denote its optimal representative set, which we assume to be unique.

unmapped: Return a set of at most min{K, ceil(H_M L)} arms with coverage loss within epsilon of the optimal size-L loss, w.p. 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: with probability at least 1-delta, the relaxed procedure returns a set \widehat S satisfying Phi(\widehat S) <= Phi(S_L^*)+epsilon, |\widehat S| <= ceil(H_M L)

symbols.Gamma_a: effective gap of arm a (Eq. effective-arm-gap), combining group-representative gaps Delta_{q,a}/(8 lambda_bar_q), objective-wise gaps g_{m,a}/4 and radius rho_q

conditions: each objective has a unique best arm
tuning: epsilon_r = 2^{-r}, delta_r = 6 delta/(pi^2 r^2), n_r = ceil(2 sigma^2/epsilon_r^2 log(2KM/delta_r))

source.label: thm:gse-sample-complexity
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:gse} returns the optimal representative tuple $\bm a_{\mathcal G}^\star$ using at most $T_{\rm GFM}(\boldsymbol\mu,\delta)$ arm pulls, where T_GFM = \widetilde O(\sigma^2\sum_{a=1}^K\frac{1}{\Gamma_a^2}\log\frac{KM}{\delta}).

results.notes: Proof gives explicit bound sum_a [1 + 8 sigma^2/Gamma_a^2 log(pi^2 KM/(3 delta) (1+ceil(log2(1/Gamma_a)))^2)]. Output is correct with prob >= 1-delta.

symbols.Gamma_La: effective gap Gamma_{L,a} of arm a in latent-group setting (Eq. latent-effective-gap)

conditions: each objective has a unique best arm

source.label: thm:afm-sample-complexity
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:afm-elim} returns the optimal representative set $S_L^\star$ using at most $T_{\rm AFM}(\boldsymbol\mu,\delta)$ arm pulls, where T_AFM = \widetilde O(\sigma^2\sum_{a=1}^K\frac{1}{\Gamma_{L,a}^2}\log\frac{KM}{\delta}).

results.notes: Compute marked exponential because the algorithm maintains the family of all binom(K,L) candidate sets; paper calls it computationally intractable in general.

symbols.T_L_star: characteristic time defined by (T_L^*)^{-1} = sup_w inf_{nu in Alt_L(mu)} sum_a w_a ||mu_a - nu_a||^2/(2 sigma^2)

source.label: thm:latent-lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1/2)$. Any fixed-confidence algorithm that identifies the optimal representative set with probability at least $1-\delta$ on every Gaussian instance with a unique optimal representative set satisfies $\mathbb E_{\boldsymbol\mu}[\tau]\geq T_L^\star(\boldsymbol\mu)\operatorname{KL}(1-\delta,\delta)$

symbols.T_L_star: characteristic time of the latent-group problem

results.notes: Asymptotic in delta (not T). Algorithm class: delta-PAC algorithms.

source.label: thm:biafm-greedy
source.quote: For any $\epsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:biafm-greedy} returns a set $\widehat S$ such that $|\widehat S|\leq\min\{K,\lceil H_ML\rceil\}$, $\Phi(\widehat S)\leq\Phi(S_L^\star)+\epsilon$ ... The total number of arm pulls satisfies T_BiAFM \leq K\lceil\frac{32\sigma^2\overline\lambda^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(\frac{2KM}{\delta})\rceil.

results.notes: Pull count is deterministic (uniform sampling); the correctness guarantee (set size <= min{K, ceil(H_M L)}, loss within epsilon) holds with prob >= 1-delta. Bicriteria (H_M, epsilon, delta)-PAC result.

bound.regime: delta -> 0, with probability tending to 1, for every eps_alg > 0

symbols.T_L_star: characteristic time of the latent-group problem

tuning: stopping threshold beta(t,delta) = log(pi^2 t^2 |S_L| /(6 delta))
forced exploration when min_a N_a(t) < sqrt(t) - K/2

source.label: thm:afm-asymptotic-optimality
source.quote: Suppose that the rewards are Gaussian and $T_L^\star(\boldsymbol\mu)<\infty$, and that the allocation oracle in Step 7 is exact. Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:afm-tas} is $\delta$-PAC and, for every $\eta>0$, satisfies $\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\mu}(\tau_\delta\leq(1+\eta)T_L^\star(\boldsymbol\mu)\log\frac{1}{\delta})=1.$

results.notes: Paper's eta (free slack) mapped to eps_alg. Guarantee is a limit in probability on the stopping time, not on its expectation. Oracle-based; computation not stated (requires exact max-min oracle).

symbols.zeta_min: minimum assignment gap over objectives within S_L^*

conditions: Assumption 1: each objective has a unique best arm within S_L^*
holds on the confidence event E (probability >= 1-delta)

source.quote: Suppose that $L\geq2$ and that Assumption~\ref{ass:unique-latent-assignment} holds. On the event $\mathcal E$, condition Eq.~(\ref{eq:assignment-stopping}) is satisfied for all objectives once $\epsilon_r<\frac{\zeta_{\min}}{4}$, and the resulting assignments and groups satisfy $\widehat\pi(m)=\pi_L^\star(m)$, $\widehat G_a=G_a^\star$. The additional sample complexity is at most \widetilde O(\frac{\sigma^2L}{\zeta_{\min}^2}\log\frac{KM}{\delta}).

results.notes: Additional samples for recovering latent groups after S_L^* has been identified by AFM-Elim.
